correctness.rationale: For n≥9 every vector has a coordinate at least 3; such coordinates are disjoint between compatible vectors, hence at most four codewords, attained by the four pure vectors. For n=3 all 20 vectors work. At n=4..8 valid witnesses have 11,6,5,5,5 elements. A complete integer-mask recursion on the full graphs of 35,56,84,120,165 compositions excludes cliques of sizes 12,7,6,6,6; it visits 7056,13027,14895,16825,19450 recursion nodes, respectively. Its enumeration covers all candidate cliques, with only a sound cardinality pruning rule. Standalone checker independently verifies disjoint actual three-survivor output sets for all witnesses. The finite experiment is an exhaustive proof for these five finite domains, not a projection to unbounded n.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broad published puncturing and incidence bounds cover this case as inequalities, but are too weak to force 11,6,5,5,5 or the exact threshold 9. Published ball-volume formulas count different objects; they do not imply maximum independent-set sizes without further arguments.

value.rationale: A current 2026 primary paper explicitly treats n−3 multiset deletions but leaves generally nonsharp bounds. Four symbols are the smallest alphabet beyond a separately resolved ternary case. The full exact finite-and-infinite optimum S_4(n,n−3), together with sharp stabilization n=9 and explicit optimal witnesses, is a natural complete extremal classification, not an arbitrary small instance or general-theorem substitution. Its finite numbers are independent nontrivial graph optima and its infinite tail provides a closing argument.
